Campaign: Adele — “All This Time” (Time Travel Concept)

Overview
A time-bending, emotionally resonant campaign that invites fans to revisit who they were, meet who they’ve become, and step forward with Adele. The creative blends nostalgia, self-reflection, and cinematic elegance, positioning Adele’s new era as a journey through past, present, and future selves.

Unique Selling Proposition (USP)
- The world’s most trusted voice in heartbreak and healing, now guiding listeners through time: one voice, countless versions of you.
- Adele’s rare authenticity meets a cinematic, interactive experience that lets fans “travel” through their own timelines with the music as the vehicle.

Emotional Hook and Core Message
- Hook: What would you say to your younger self—and what would she say back?
- Core message: Some songs don’t just play. They take you back—and bring you forward.
- Desired feelings: catharsis, permission to feel, hope, closure, awe.

Target Audience
- Primary: Women 25–44; emotionally driven music fans seeking reflection, resilience, and connection.
- Secondary: Gen Z and Millennials (18–34) across TikTok/Instagram who love nostalgic storytelling and cinematic aesthetics.
- Tertiary: Cross-generational mainstream listeners drawn to timeless vocals and big cultural moments.

Tone and Visual Identity
- Tone: Intimate, elegant, grounded; quietly epic.
- Palette: Midnight blue, soft gold, ivory; accents of candlelight amber.
- Visual cues: Hourglasses, film grain, soft lens flares, watch dials, mirrors; slow-motion dust motes. Fashion: classic silhouettes, black silk, tailored coats.

Campaign Slogans and Hashtags
- Primary tagline: All This Time.
- Support lines:
  - Some songs don’t just play—they take you back.
  - If you could sing to your past, what would you say?
  - Time doesn’t heal everything. But it helps you sing it.
- Hashtags: #AllThisTime, #AdeleThroughTime, #LettersToMyself

Campaign Pillars
1) Timelines: Adele revisits past eras to launch the future one.
2) Letters to Myself: Fans and creators share messages to past/future selves set to snippets.
3) The Time Rooms: Immersive, IRL pop-ups that let fans walk through different “years” of sound and memory.
4) Timekeeper Tech: Interactive web and AR experiences that “dial” to moments in your life.

Launch Phases
- Tease (T-14 to T-7):
  - 10-second cryptic spot: ticking, a soft gold watch face; Adele’s silhouette; line: “All this time.”
  - Instagram grid blackout to midnight blue; story posts with dates on watch dials.
  - Times Square and Piccadilly screens: an hourglass filling in reverse; zero copy except “Soon.”
- Reveal (T-7 to T-1):
  - Artwork reveal: Adele in profile, doubled like a reflection across time. Caption: “Some songs take you back.”
  - Pre-save launch; interactive site “Dial Back” goes live.
  - Press photos and interview tease focused on growth, closure, and time.
- Drop (Launch Day):
  - Premiere music video with time-shifted vignettes.
  - The Time Rooms open in London and Los Angeles (48 hours only).
  - TikTok Sounds release; creator seeding for #LettersToMyself.
- Sustain (Weeks 1–4):
  - Live acoustic performances from iconic, time-significant venues.
  - Behind-the-scenes “making of” the time concept.
  - Fan story spotlights edited into official “All This Time” montage.

Hero Film: 60-Second Video Ad Script (TV/YouTube Pre-Roll)
- Visual: A dim hallway lined with doors labeled by years. Soft grain, candlelight glow.
- SFX: A steady tick that blends into a soft piano chord.
- Adele (VO, intimate): “If I could sing to the girl I was… and the woman I’ve become…”
- Visual: Adele opens “2011.” A living room. A younger version of herself flickers on a TV. She smiles—bittersweet.
- Music: First chorus line swells (new single hook).
- Visual: Cut to “2024.” She steps through rain on a neon-lit street; time slows. People pass in double exposure.
- Adele (VO): “Some songs don’t just play. They take you back.”
- Visual: The hourglass tips; the sand floats upward. She reaches into a mirror; her future hand meets hers.
- Hook lyric hits; camera pushes in.
- On-screen text: All This Time.
- Adele (gentle breath): “Shall we?”
- End slate: Pre-save now. Midnight Friday. #AllThisTime

Social Media Ad Concepts
- Instagram Reels (15s): Adele closes a watch; a muffled heartbeat syncs with ticks. Text overlay: “If you could send a song back, which year needs it?” CTA: Pre-save.
- Instagram Carousel: 4 frames labeled 2011, 2015, 2021, Now—each frame shows a visual motif and a lyric fragment. Final panel: “All This Time. Pre-save today.”
- TikTok Prompt: #LettersToMyself. Creators speak one line to their past self; smash cut to lip-sync of the hook. CTA: Use sound, tag #AdeleThroughTime.
- TikTok Effect: “Time Dial” AR—drag to select a year, color grade shifts to that era; a 10s snippet auto-matches the vibe. Sticker: “Sent with love from your future.”
- X (Twitter) Teasers:
  - “Some apologies arrive right on time. Some arrive years late. I wrote both. — A”
  - “To the girl who thought this was the end. It was the beginning. #AllThisTime”

OOH and Billboard Concepts
- Visual: Minimalist hourglass in soft gold on midnight blue; Adele’s silhouette inside the glass.
- Headline options:
  - All This Time.
  - Some songs bring you back to move you forward.
  - Time doesn’t heal everything. But it helps you sing it.
- CTA: Midnight Friday. Pre-save now. QR code.

Search and Display Ads
- Search:
  - Headline 1: Adele — All This Time
  - Headline 2: New Music. A New Chapter.
  - Description: Some songs don’t just play—they take you back. Pre-save the new single now.
- Display banners:
  - Visual: Watch dial with lyric etched on glass.
  - Copy: “If you could sing to your past, what would you say?” Button: Pre-save.

Email Marketing Copy
- Subject line options:
  - All This Time — a note from Adele
  - Tonight at midnight. Let’s go back.
- Body (Announcement):
  - I’ve been thinking about the things we’d say to our younger selves—what we’d forgive, what we’d keep. This is a song for those conversations. Pre-save All This Time and I’ll see you at midnight.
  - CTA: Pre-save on Spotify / Apple Music
- Body (Eve of Release):
  - Midnight is closer than it feels. Put the kettle on. Let’s go back—together.
  - CTA: Watch the premiere
- Body (Morning After):
  - For every memory that still aches and every future you’re brave enough to try—thank you for listening.
  - CTA: Stream now

Landing Page Copy (Pre-Save Hub)
- Headline: All This Time.
- Subhead: Some songs don’t just play—they take you back.
- Body: Pre-save the new single, unlock a message from Adele, and dial back to the year that changed you.
- Interactive: Year selector wheel; choosing a year reveals a personalized lyric line and aesthetic shift.
- CTAs: Pre-save on Spotify / Apple Music; Get SMS reminder; Explore The Time Rooms
- Social proof: “A voice that never ages—only deepens.” — Pull-quote block in elegant serif.

Influencer and Creator Strategy
- Partner tiers: Storyteller creators, poets, mental-health advocates, filmmakers, fashion and nostalgia accounts.
- Brief: Share a 20–30s #LettersToMyself piece—one truth you’d send back in time. Use the official sound. Keep it intimate and unpolished.
- Paid seed examples:
  - “I forgive you for not knowing better.” Cut to hook.
  - “You were not hard to love. You were tired.” Cut to hook.
- Music storytellers produce “eras” edits—styling and color-grading looks to match different years, then transition into present-day confidence.

Experiential: The Time Rooms (Pop-Up)
- Location: London + Los Angeles, 48 hours.
- Rooms:
  1) The Beginning: Warm living room vignette with vinyl crackle; Polaroids projected in motion.
  2) The Storm: Rain room with glass reflections and doubled silhouettes.
  3) The Mirror: Infinity mirrors with floating lyric fragments in soft gold.
  4) The Horizon: Dawn light; a single piano. Guests record a 10s message to their past/future selves; receive it via email “in one year.”
- Mechanics: Entry via pre-save confirmation; QR codes to capture UGC; staff photographer for cinematic portraits.

PR Angles and Content
- Long lead: “Bending Time: How Adele turns nostalgia into healing.”
- Short lead: “Letters to My Younger Self: Fans join Adele for a global time-capsule.”
- BTS featurette: The making of the time motif—musical references, instrument choices, and visual symbolism.

Creative Direction Notes
- Typography: Elegant serif for headings, soft sans for body. Kerning slightly expanded; generous negative space.
- Motion language: Gentle dissolves, match cuts, mirrored transitions; sand turning to starlight.
- Sound design: Ticks morphing into heartbeat, then piano. Sub-bass swells at transitions.

Calls-to-Action (CTAs)
- Pre-save now
- Watch the premiere
- Visit The Time Rooms
- Share your #LettersToMyself
- Text REMEMBER to [shortcode] for release SMS reminder

KPIs and Measurement
- Pre-saves and add-to-library rates (target: top-decile for prior releases)
- First 24-hour streams and MV views
- UGC volume on #LettersToMyself and #AdeleThroughTime
- Time Rooms attendance and QR interactions
- Earned media volume and sentiment
- Watch-through rates on hero film; click-through on display and social

Optional Print Ad Concepts
- Full-bleed portrait, soft grain, candle-lit edge light.
- Copy variants:
  - “What would you tell the person you were when you first heard me?”
  - “All This Time. Midnight Friday.”
  - Minimal footer: Pre-save. adele.com

This campaign preserves Adele’s intimate authenticity while expanding her universe with a cinematic, time-travel metaphor—turning release day into a shared moment of reflection, healing, and forward motion.

Title: The Ultimate Guide to Mediterranean Diet Recipes

Meta description: Discover the Mediterranean diet with easy recipes, healthy eating tips, and meal plans. Build a delicious, sustainable routine with simple, flavor-packed Mediterranean meals.

Introduction: Why the Mediterranean diet makes healthy eating feel effortless
Healthy eating should feel joyful, not restrictive. The Mediterranean diet celebrates color, freshness, and flavor—ripe tomatoes, peppery olive oil, sun-sweet citrus, fragrant herbs—while supporting long-term well-being. This guide gives you easy recipes, pantry essentials, and quick meal formulas so you can eat better without sacrificing taste or time.

What is the Mediterranean diet?
- A way of eating inspired by countries bordering the Mediterranean Sea.
- Built around vegetables, fruits, whole grains, legumes, nuts, seeds, olive oil, fish, and modest dairy.
- Light on red meat, highly processed foods, and added sugars.
- Enjoyed with movement, community, and mindful eating.

Benefits at a glance
- Heart-friendly: Emphasis on olive oil, fish, and fiber-rich plants.
- Satisfying and sustainable: Balanced fats and fiber keep you full.
- Flexible and flavorful: Easy to adapt for busy schedules, families, and various dietary preferences.
Note: Always consult a healthcare professional for personalized nutrition guidance.

Mediterranean pantry staples (stock these once, cook easily all week)
- Oils, acids, aromatics: Extra-virgin olive oil, red wine vinegar, lemon, garlic, onions.
- Herbs and spices: Oregano, basil, parsley, thyme, cumin, smoked paprika, black pepper.
- Grains: Whole-wheat pasta, farro, quinoa, brown rice, couscous.
- Proteins: Canned chickpeas, white beans, lentils, tuna, salmon, eggs, plain Greek yogurt.
- Veggies and fruit: Tomatoes (fresh and canned), cucumbers, leafy greens, bell peppers, zucchini, eggplant, olives, citrus, berries.
- Extras: Feta, capers, tahini, nuts (almonds, pistachios, walnuts), seeds.

How to build a Mediterranean plate (the 3–2–1 formula)
- 3 parts plants: Fill at least half your plate with vegetables and fruit.
- 2 parts whole grains or legumes: Add fiber and staying power.
- 1 part protein and healthy fat: Fish, beans, eggs, or yogurt + olive oil, nuts, or avocado.
Season generously with herbs, citrus, and a drizzle of olive oil.

7 easy Mediterranean diet recipes (weeknight-friendly)

1) 10-Minute Greek Chickpea Salad
Why you’ll love it: No cooking, big flavor, perfect for meal prep.
Ingredients:
- 1 can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cucumber, chopped; 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1/4 red onion, thinly sliced; 1/3 cup kalamata olives, halved
- 1/3 cup crumbled feta; handful fresh parsley
- Dressing: 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp red wine vinegar, juice of 1/2 lemon, 1 tsp dried oregano, salt, pepper
Directions:
- Toss all ingredients with dressing. Rest 5 minutes. Serve over greens or with whole-wheat pita.

2) One-Pan Lemon Herb Salmon with Olives
Why you’ll love it: Restaurant-worthy, minimal cleanup.
Ingredients:
- 2 salmon fillets; 1 zucchini (sliced), 1 bell pepper (sliced), 1 cup cherry tomatoes
- 1/3 cup olives; 2 tbsp olive oil; 1 lemon (zest + slices)
- 1 tsp each oregano and thyme; salt, pepper
Directions:
- Heat oven to 400°F (205°C). Toss vegetables with 1 tbsp oil, half the herbs, salt, pepper. Spread on a sheet pan.
- Nestle salmon on top. Drizzle remaining oil, add zest, herbs, lemon slices, olives.
- Roast 12–14 minutes until salmon flakes. Finish with a squeeze of lemon.

3) Creamy Tomato-Basil Lentil Soup
Why you’ll love it: Hearty, budget-friendly, freezer-friendly.
Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil; 1 onion (chopped); 2 garlic cloves (minced)
- 1 tsp smoked paprika; 1 tsp dried basil
- 1 cup red lentils (rinsed); 1 can crushed tomatoes; 4 cups low-sodium vegetable broth
- 1/3 cup plain Greek yogurt (or coconut milk), salt, pepper, fresh basil to finish
Directions:
- Sauté onion and garlic in oil until soft. Add spices, toast 30 seconds.
- Stir in lentils, tomatoes, broth. Simmer 18–20 minutes until lentils are tender.
- Stir in yogurt, salt, pepper. Top with basil and a drizzle of olive oil.

4) Mediterranean Sheet-Pan Chicken and Veggies
Why you’ll love it: Family-friendly, great for leftovers.
Ingredients:
- 4 boneless chicken thighs; 1 red onion (wedges); 1 eggplant (chunks); 1 zucchini (chunks); 1 cup cherry tomatoes
- Marinade: 3 tbsp olive oil, juice of 1 lemon, 2 tsp oregano, 1 tsp cumin, 3 minced garlic cloves, salt, pepper
Directions:
- Heat oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss chicken and veggies with marinade. Spread on a sheet pan.
- Roast 25–30 minutes, flipping once. Serve with quinoa or whole-wheat couscous.

5) Whole-Wheat Pasta with Burst Tomatoes, Spinach, and Feta
Why you’ll love it: Comforting, fast, pantry-based.
Ingredients:
- 8 oz whole-wheat spaghetti; 2 tbsp olive oil; 3 garlic cloves (sliced)
- 2 cups cherry tomatoes; 4 cups baby spinach; 1/3 cup feta; pinch red pepper flakes; salt, pepper
Directions:
- Cook pasta. Meanwhile, warm oil, sauté garlic 30 seconds. Add tomatoes and pinch salt; cook until they burst.
- Toss in spinach to wilt. Add pasta, feta, pepper flakes, and pasta water as needed to gloss. Finish with black pepper and olive oil.

6) Herby Yogurt Breakfast Bowl
Why you’ll love it: Savory breakfast that keeps you full.
Ingredients:
- 3/4 cup plain Greek yogurt; 1/2 cup chopped cucumber and tomato
- 1 tsp olive oil; lemon zest; chopped dill or parsley; pinch za’atar or oregano; salt, pepper
Directions:
- Stir herbs, zest, and oil into yogurt. Top with cucumber, tomato, and seasoning. Serve with whole-grain toast.

Snack and dip ideas (5 minutes or less)
- Classic hummus with carrot sticks and olives
- Apple slices with tahini and sesame seeds
- Whole-grain toast with mashed avocado, lemon, and chili flakes
- Cottage cheese or Greek yogurt with olive oil, cherry tomatoes, and black pepper
- Mixed nuts with dried figs or apricots

3-day Mediterranean meal plan (easy, flexible)

Day 1
- Breakfast: Herby yogurt bowl
- Lunch: Greek chickpea salad + whole-wheat pita
- Snack: Hummus with cucumbers
- Dinner: Lemon herb salmon with olives + farro

Day 2
- Breakfast: Oats cooked in milk with walnuts, cinnamon, and berries
- Lunch: Leftover salmon flaked over greens with lemon-olive oil dressing
- Snack: Apple with tahini
- Dinner: Sheet-pan chicken and veggies + brown rice

Day 3
- Breakfast: Avocado toast with tomato and feta
- Lunch: Tomato-basil lentil soup + side salad
- Snack: Cottage cheese with tomatoes and olive oil
- Dinner: Whole-wheat pasta with burst tomatoes and spinach

Meal prep tips for easy recipes and healthy eating
- Batch-cook a grain: Make a pot of quinoa or farro on Sunday.
- Roast a tray of mixed vegetables: Use through the week in salads, bowls, omelets.
- Make two dressings: Lemon-oregano vinaigrette and tahini-lemon sauce to transform leftovers.
- Pre-portion snacks: Nuts, cut veggies, and hummus cups.
- Keep quick proteins handy: Canned tuna, chickpeas, eggs, and Greek yogurt.

Budget and time savers
- Buy in-season produce and frozen vegetables for consistent quality and price.
- Use canned beans, tomatoes, and fish—nutritious and affordable.
- Choose whole grains in bulk; cook once, eat twice.
- Embrace “template” meals: Grain + veg + protein + olive oil + herbs.

Vegetarian and vegan swaps
- Replace fish or chicken with chickpeas, lentils, or tofu.
- Use dairy-free yogurt or coconut milk in soups and sauces.
- Lean on tahini, nuts, and olive oil for satisfying healthy fats.

Grocery list starter
- Produce: Leafy greens, cucumbers, tomatoes, onions, bell peppers, zucchini, eggplant, lemons, berries.
- Proteins: Eggs, Greek yogurt, canned chickpeas, lentils, tuna or salmon.
- Grains: Whole-wheat pasta, quinoa, farro, brown rice, whole-grain bread or pita.
- Pantry: Extra-virgin olive oil, red wine vinegar, olives, capers, canned tomatoes, tahini.
- Flavor: Garlic, fresh parsley/dill/basil, oregano, cumin, paprika, black pepper, chili flakes.
- Extras: Feta, nuts, seeds.

Your next step
- Pick two recipes from this guide and add the ingredients to your next grocery run.
- Use the 3–2–1 plate formula to build balanced meals all week.
- Want more? Save this guide and share it with a friend who’s ready for delicious, healthy eating the Mediterranean way.

Core message and emotional hook
- Unique value: The Mediterranean diet makes healthy eating easy, flavorful, and sustainable with simple, accessible ingredients.
- Emotional hook: Turn mealtime into an everyday pleasure—vibrant, satisfying dishes that love you back.
- Call to action: Start with one recipe today and feel the difference by dinner.
